problem: Material work could stop at commits, open PRs, queued CI, stopped chats, timeouts or lost workers while multiple agents created parallel delivery state. GitHub Actions additionally accumulated stale PR-head runs because top-level workflows either had no concurrency guard or keyed concurrency on the candidate SHA itself.
root_cause: Repository hygiene and universal ingress existed, but no single cross-surface lifecycle/recovery contract made incomplete execution non-terminal and finishing-first across agent/chat/GitHub/runtime boundaries. For GitHub Actions, SHA-scoped concurrency made every new head a new concurrency group, so cancel-in-progress could not supersede older heads; other fan-out workflows had no PR single-flight guard at all. A second observed failure mode was operational misclassification: an implementation candidate in WAITING_CAPACITY/FINISH_EXISTING_WORK_FIRST can look like a runner or CI blockage while admission is intentionally yielding to a live recovery candidate. During recovery, a source refactor also exposed a stale test oracle: the approved-blog wrapper delegated implementation to publish_approved_blog_v2_core.py while change-scoped release tests still asserted implementation symbols in the thin wrapper.
prevention: one obligation, one active executable candidate
incomplete delivery/runtime states are recoverable, never terminal
durable heartbeat/lease/checkpoint plus idempotent readback before retry
finish existing admitted work before lower-priority starts under capacity pressure
queued or in-progress GitHub Actions are WAIT states and must never trigger retry/no-op/retrigger commits
all top-level PR fan-out workflows use PR-scoped single-flight concurrency with cancel-in-progress=true
candidate SHA remains an exact-head verification input inside delivery gates, never the PR concurrency identity
freeze the current candidate while checks are queued, pending or in-progress; mutate only after terminal defect evidence
before repairing CI, classify the blocker as admission, deterministic test failure, transient runner/platform failure, stale/superseded run or external dependency
if finish-before-start is caused by a live recovery candidate, finish or deterministically supersede that recovery first; never bypass the admission rule to make the implementation candidate run
after any recovery merge or main movement, reread current main, candidate head, PR metadata and current workflow state before acting so stale failures never become repair authority
for a real failing job, isolate the first concrete assertion/contract break from the current exact-head run and repair only that cause on the same canonical lineage

after a source refactor moves implementation behind a thin wrapper, tests must assert implementation contracts at the canonical implementation boundary and wrapper contracts only at the wrapper boundary

PR_HEAD_SHA_DRIFT is a valid fail-closed signal: if the live PR head moves while a run is evaluating an older SHA, discard that run as promotion authority and restart reasoning from the new exact head
declared delivery metadata must be reconciled after legitimate main/head lineage movement rather than weakening exact-head or identity checks
normalize GitHub delivery telemetry into deterministic learning evidence
promote repeated learnings into regression tests, gates or guardrails
canonical_loop: intent -> preflight -> admission -> execute -> verify -> protected merge -> deploy -> production readback -> outcome -> learning -> prevention -> fulfilled

evidence.finding: central Required/Unified jobs were queued before first runner step, proving pre-run capacity rather than a product-test failure

after PR-single-flight was added to the fan-out workflows, newer head creation caused Brain foundation, Shared Agent Memory, BG168, Learning Classifier, CodeQL, Powerhouse CodeQL, Engineering Intelligence and Engineering Supply Chain runs for the stale head to finish as cancelled
requires all ten known PR fan-out workflows to key concurrency on pull-request identity, cancel stale work, and preserve exact-head verification in Required/Unified

PR #1968 was intentionally held because recovery PR #1970 was the live recovery candidate. The correct action was to trace and finish the recovery candidate rather than weaken admission or blindly rerun implementation CI.

Required test and BRAIN delivery shared the same stale test-oracle failure: tests searched implementation symbols such as faq_items and source_contract in the thin publish_approved_blog_v2.py wrapper after those implementations had moved to scripts/brain/publish_approved_blog_v2_core.py. The repair updated the oracle at the implementation boundary without broad product changes.
Required test and BRAIN delivery reached terminal SUCCESS on the same exact head before protected merge; older failed runs were ignored as stale evidence.
the recovery candidate completed through protected merge with expected-head identity and main readback, proving the finish-before-start blocker was recoverable work, not a terminal CI/runner blockage
after #1970 completion, #1968 was automatically admitted again by the existing hygiene/admission gate and preflight started; no admission bypass was used
when the live #1968 head moved during an older Required attempt, the control plane emitted PR_HEAD_SHA_DRIFT and rejected the stale run as authority. This behavior is correct and must be preserved.

main advanced through follow-up learning work; PR #1968 was reread afterward and remained open/mergeable on the current lineage. Subsequent candidate heads must always supersede the concrete SHAs recorded here for promotion decisions.
human-readable incident, root-cause, recovery and prevention record linked to the same powerhouse-one-loop-v1 obligation; it complements rather than duplicates this machine-readable learning
